gaps.sentence: As soon as I turned eighteen, I ___ get a driving licence.
gaps.explanation: For a particular permitted act, 'was allowed to' is preferred: was allowed to.

gaps.sentence: It is Saturday tomorrow, so I ___ get up early.
gaps.hint: an absence of obligation at weekends
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' shows there is no obligation: don't have to get up.

gaps.sentence: You ___ pay for children under six — entry is free for them.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' expresses absence of necessity: needn't pay.

gaps.sentence: The report ___ have been finished yesterday; the deadline was missed.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have been finished' — it was expected but did not happen.

gaps.sentence: If I were you, I ___ take the earlier train.
gaps.hint: if I were you plus would
gaps.explanation: 'If I were you' is followed by 'would': would take.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather stay in tonight, if that's all right.
The medicine ___ be kept out of the reach of children.
gaps.explanation: Written instructions use 'must' for essential requirements: must be kept.

gaps.sentence: I ___ work late every Wednesday this month; it is a new company policy.
gaps.hint: obligation imposed by an external rule
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' expresses obligation imposed by external rules: have to work.
